fields.why: The headline claims compare real-time trend categories with later ED data (comparison), but single-quantity results are also reported (e.g. national ED percentage 0.3%, peak 2.6%), so adding summary is defensible; B's list is slightly fuller.

The posterior probability that Rt>1 is binned by fixed cutoffs into the trend categories, which are the indicator being evaluated: this is quantization of an EpiNow2 output, not a test of a hypothesis. No CI is reported and the brief says nothing about Bayesian exceedance probabilities; B itself offered quantization as the alternative reading.
Follows from procedure_classes: no named test, p-value or CI-vs-null judgment appears in the article.

The trend categories and ED visits are compared across four time points (and jurisdictions in the table), which is a group of 3 or more periods. A's referents do not hold: Rt=1 is a classification cutpoint, and the final ED data are a later measurement used like a reference standard, not a fixed target or population value.
No CIs or tests are reported. The probability-based categories are model outputs used as the indicator, so they are not a test; see procedure_classes.

brief_issues: Brief needs a rule for Bayesian posterior probabilities against a fixed value (e.g. P(Rt>1) categories): say whether they count as a test, like CI vs fixed value, or as quantization of a model output. It also needs to say whether, in a nowcast/indicator evaluation, comparing the indicator with later complete data is a comparison or a reference standard.
